That deferral has expired — **V1's tool set is two standalone tools**, the **document creator** (T-335) and the **QA checker** (T-336), and this ticket is the launcher they live in. **Assembled from entitlements, not filtered** — the T-269 rule applies to tools exactly as to workers: an unentitled tool is *absent*, never disabled, so the section never advertises a capability the viewer cannot use. Infora-standard tools only; org-built and user-built tools are the builder, `Q-014`, and stay post-V1. | *(Deps: T-269)*
- **T-335 — Document creator: the structure-first authoring surface.** The owner's V1 tool set, half one: *"rather than drafting a document using the editor/chat interface, you build the structure of a document, define what content you want in it, and the sources it will draw from in the library."* **T-309 builds the DAG; this builds the thing a user actually operates** — compose the outline, state the intent for each section, and **bind library sources per section before anything generates**. The ordering is the design: sources are chosen *ahead* of drafting, so the run has an explicit source manifest rather than a retrieval guess, which is what makes the output auditable against what the author asked for. Reached from Tools (T-334). **Open where it meets the deliverable plan:** whether a bound container's TIDP metadata seeds the structure is not ruled — do not invent it here. | *(Deps: T-309, T-334)*
- 🌫 **Fog — the QA checker as a tool and its run.** Real work, deliberately **not ticketed**, because it cannot yet be *specified* — only *stated*, which is what `Q-031` does. The owner ruled the checker a **bulk review**: a batch sweep producing many marks in one run, where the editor's agent is incremental with a human in the loop each turn. **Nothing in the build has a bulk mode**, and four things trade against each other — the unit of work, the scope of a run, the cost envelope (one sweep is not one model call), and triage at volume, which collides with ADR-0048 §3's no-bulk-accept guard. **Ticket it when `Q-031` is ruled.** *(T-336 was minted for this on 2026-08-01 and withdrawn the same day under the rule above; the number is a deliberate gap and is not reused.)*

**Slice V1-S — The schema import assistant** *(owner-ruled 2026-08-03. T-337–T-338.)* The **first assistive agent embedded in a surface** rather than launched as a tool, and the only one of three candidates weighed on 2026-08-02 that enters V1. The other two are recorded here so the reasoning is not re-derived: a **review-cycle preflight** is almost entirely *doing* under ADR-0027 — reviewer slots filled, a lead reviewer present, author not also lead reviewer — so it is a **validator, not an agent**, and its judgement residue is thin enough to name only once the validator exists; a **sandbox reorganiser** is substantially Slice O P2, which [v1.md](v1.md) defers, and is blocked twice over by `Q-020` (whether sandbox material may enter agent context at all) and `Q-031` (it is a third instance of the unruled bulk mode). This slice needs no content pack because it **transcribes the user's own file rather than advising** — which is exactly why it could be specified while `Q-034` stays open.

- **T-337 — Schema import: a spreadsheet becomes candidate fields.** Every consultancy already has its schema in a spreadsheet, and [schema.tsx](../../apps/web/src/screens/schema.tsx)'s `OptionsEditor` — a code and a description typed per row, built to scale to "the long routewide code lists" — makes retyping it the highest-friction moment in the product, landing in the pilot's *first hour* before the firm has seen a single benefit. **Deterministic-first, ADR-0027 §2 pattern 1** (code with an LLM escape hatch): a CSV or XLSX whose headers are recognisable maps to `NamingSchemeField` with **no model call at all**, and only unrecognised columns escalate to `extractor` (T-274) rather than growing a second extraction path. The deterministic half is useful alone, which is what keeps this off Phase B's critical path. **No migration** — the upload is parsed in-request and the result is written through the existing naming-scheme `PUT`. Three hard constraints: (1) the file is **never admitted to the library**, never chunked, never retrievable — it is not corpus and must not touch the ingest path; (2) **the run request must not echo the file body**, because `runs.request` is persisted and an existing schema routinely carries **named people** in its author and reviewer columns, so echoing the upload would silently create a personal-data store ([personal-data.md](personal-data.md)); (3) an unparseable file **fails loudly and names the row**, matching V1's per-document ingest ruling. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-338 — The schema surface accepts an import and stages it for review.** Upload on the deliverable-schema screen; the parsed fields land **in the editing table, unsaved**, for the owner to check row by row before `Save schema`. **Nothing is auto-applied, and the guarantee comes free** — the owner already holds the write and the table is already an editor, so the import gains **no write path the owner did not already have**, which is ADR-0048 §3's principle arriving without new machinery. **A diff, never a silent replace:** the table states what the import would add, change and drop, because `Reset to Infora default` already sits beside it and an import that quietly wiped a schema in progress is the same accident with a worse cause. **Scoped to `canEdit` (the owner super-user) in V1** — a guest super-user's import would have to become `NamingProposal` rows, whose `body` is free text and cannot carry a field list. That is a deliberate scope cut, recorded so it is not later read as an oversight. | *(Deps: T-337)*

**Slice V1-P — The privacy programme** *(ruled 2026-08-03, design session 4 → [ADR-0050](../adr/0050-the-privacy-programme-operator-access-and-deletion.md), closing `Q-032` and `Q-033`. T-339–T-342.)* What the pilot firm's DPA is written against, and the first written position Infora has ever held on **its own** access to customer data. Two halves: the operator path, which is infrastructure and rides Slice V1-I; and deletion, which is product and has never existed — `DELETE /sandbox-documents/:id` is a *soft* delete with self-service restore (T-128), and nothing in the controlled library can be removed by anyone at all. **The exit export is deliberately not ticketed** — ADR-0050 §8 specifies it (documents as files plus the review record in readable form), but it is needed when a contract *ends*, so it is **post-V1** and named in Slice C rather than minted here.

- **T-339 — The break-glass access path: no standing human credential.** The Terraform half of ADR-0050 §1, and the claim the DPA makes. **Two roles, and conflating them is the failure this ticket exists to prevent:** the **pipeline role** stays as ADR-0047 §9 built it — non-human, assumable only by GitHub Actions via OIDC, running migrations as a one-off task, **with no interactive session possible**; and a new **human break-glass role**, assumable by a named person only, **time-bounded** (short session duration, enforced by the role's own trust policy rather than by convention), requiring a **stated reason** recorded at assume-time, with **CloudTrail** as the out-of-band record the assuming party cannot edit. **No standing IAM user, no long-lived key, no console password on any human principal** — the credential that cannot be leaked is the one never minted (§7's rule, extended to people). **Done when:** an access report for a given customer and window can be produced from CloudTrail alone, because that is what the DPA promises on request; and a test asserts the break-glass role cannot be assumed without a reason string. | *(Deps: T-316)*
- **T-340 — Purge: the deletion act the product has never had.** ADR-0050 §5–§6. **Delete stays exactly as T-128 built it** — the bin, restorable, self-service. **Purge** is the second act: genuinely erases, **reaches the derived stores**, org-admin only, behind a typed confirmation, recorded with a named actor. **The derived half is the whole ticket** — a purge that deletes the row and leaves `version_chunks` has erased nothing, since the text survives in the retrieval index; and S3 versioning is **on** (ADR-0047 §3), so a delete writes a *delete-marker* and real erasure needs a version-level purge. **Bounded by whose material it is, not by where it sits:** reaches the member organisation's own material — sandbox and personal-sandbox documents, org context, drafts, its own producer-private Runs, Signals, cost attribution, its conflict register — and **never** anything promoted into the library, which is T-341's path. **Done when:** a purged document's text is unfindable by retrieval *and* by direct chunk query, the S3 object has no recoverable version, and a run that cited it reports T-253's `unreconstructable` rather than a silent gap. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-341 — Library removal: withdraw, then the owner organisation removes.** ADR-0050 §7, and the answer to the realistic V1 incident — the first real corpus load is also the first real test, so a document belonging to a *different client* going in is the failure to design for. **Two steps, and the first is already built:** `containers.state = 'live'` is a pre-filter *inside* the retrieval query ([retrieval.ts:90](../../packages/knowledge/src/retrieval.ts#L90)), so **withdraw already stops grounding** in the same statement as the wall — no work. This ticket is the second step: the **owner organisation** removes a **withdrawn** container from the library, **on request from the producing organisation**. **The authority is the point** — the lever sits with the party whose library it is (ADR-0016; ADR-0026 Filter 1), and putting it in the producing firm's hand would let a consultancy erase six months of corpus ahead of a dispute, leaving every citation in every accepted deliverable resolving to nothing. **Removal means erased, not delisted** — same derived-store reach as T-340. **Refused on a container that is not withdrawn**, so the two steps cannot be collapsed into one click. | *(Deps: T-340)*
- **T-342 — The conflict register's `reason`: narrow its purpose on screen.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-04** (no migration, no contract change — the guidance beside the field in the T-246 declaration panel: placeholder *"Why — the fact, not the client"* plus a hint naming a worked example, *"bid team conflict" rather than naming the other side*, and stating that it is kept for whoever reviews the wall later, which is why the field survives at all). ADR-0050 §3's minimisation half, and the cheapest real reduction available. `conflict_exclusions.reason` is nullable free text ([drawer1-parties.ts:196](../../packages/db/src/schema/drawer1-parties.ts#L196)) and is the **single field that turns "a person and two project ids" into a client roster** — which matters because ADR-0046 §7 puts the register on the ADR-0018 private floor while a break-glass operator reads it regardless, and encryption was rejected on a finding (the operator controls the deployment and therefore the key). **The field stays** — a compliance partner reviewing a two-year-old wall needs the why. What changes is the guidance beside it in the T-246 declaration panel: **record the fact, not the client.** Small, and it is the difference between a useful note and a disclosure. | *(Deps: none)*

**Slice B — The Word add-in** *(design settled, component 8; converges with Slice A3 P4).* The consultant authoring surface: tracked-changes suggestions with citation + rationale, accept/edit/reject as Signals, central M365 deployment. Needs Slice A's promotion path to be fully useful, but drafting on sandbox documents can land earlier.

**Slice C — Governance depth** *(part open: threshold tuning, retention/export — bucket A).* Rails as scoped records with the ADR-0030 intersection engine, grounding-threshold calibration, withheld-output UX, audit retention/export, user-UI-action audit sense. **Plus the contract-end export** (ADR-0050 §8), specified but deliberately post-V1: the customer's documents as files in their folder structure **plus the review record in readable form** — not a database dump, and not files alone, which would hand back the documents and discard the evidence they were properly produced. No export path exists today; it is named here rather than discovered when a contract ends, and it converges with this slice's audit-export half.

**Slice D — Retrieval maturity** *(gate: Session 6 finish).* Contextual retrieval ("x in the context of y"), real channel ranking and budget, org-vs-programme precedence, per-viewer citation rendering — behind the unchanged ADR-0029 signature.

**Slice E — The moat loop** *(gate: Sessions 4, 5, 7 — must-grill, the cross-org confidentiality forks).* Org/programme context stores and drawers, the distillation engine with the ADR-0026 destination rule, precedent selection, the Signal sink, guidance notes (ADR pending), and the ADR-0026 within-tenant/cross-tenant training reconciliation flagged in the tracker.

**Slice F — Build-your-own** *(gate: Engine §5 opens — builder interface, tightening validation, sharing).* Custom tools (the Tools surface, T-109) and org-built agents: authoring through the builder in Tools, org-context storage, deploy-time rails inheritance, pre-deploy validation. The tool-scoping ruling (2026-07-13) and the wall-clean-definition stress test are on the tracker's builder theme.

**Slice G — Breadth surfaces** *(bucket A, reference-decidable).* Workspace home vs project home layout, the owner/client portfolio "control tower", programme views, mobile scope.

**Slice H — Connectors** *(deferred until the wedge is proven).* Integrate-configuration handover to an incumbent DMS; spatial/CAD/BIM by reference.

**Gate before any external pilot — the infra/security decision session** *(bucket C, component 1).* Cloud provider, blob/object storage for renditions, hosting and deployment, encryption and key management, tenant isolation, residency, production identity (replacing the skeleton auth above). The skeleton deliberately runs on the dev substrate until this is held.
